copper-scroll.name: Copper Scroll
copper-scroll.note: A list of hidden treasures engraved on copper, found in Qumran Cave 3 in 1952 (first century AD). It appears to name a place Beth Eshdatayin, often linked with the pool of Bethesda (John 5:2).

gospel-of-the-nazarenes.name: Gospel of the Nazarenes
gospel-of-the-nazarenes.note: A lost Jewish-Christian gospel in Aramaic or Syriac, close to Matthew, known only from quotations in Jerome and other church writers (300s–400s). Jerome cites its sayings as from the Gospel "according to the Hebrews"; modern scholars sort the Jewish-Christian gospel fragments into this work, the Gospel of the Hebrews and the Gospel of the Ebionites.

gospel-of-the-ebionites.name: Gospel of the Ebionites
gospel-of-the-ebionites.note: A lost Greek Jewish-Christian gospel (100s), known only from quotations in Epiphanius, Panarion 30; it blends Matthew, Mark and Luke and makes John the Baptist and Jesus vegetarian.

protevangelium-of-james.name: Protevangelium of James
protevangelium-of-james.note: A Greek story of Mary's birth and childhood and of Jesus' birth (about AD 150), the source of the names Joachim and Anna and of the view that Jesus' brothers were Joseph's sons by an earlier marriage.

toledot-yeshu.name: Toledot Yeshu
toledot-yeshu.note: A medieval Jewish counter-story of Jesus' life, in many versions, written in reaction to Christian claims and persecution; it repeats the charge of illegitimacy.

community-rule.name: Community Rule
community-rule.note: The rule book of the community at Qumran, found in Cave 1 in 1947 (copied about 100–75 BC); it applies Isaiah 40:3 to the community's withdrawal into the wilderness.

war-scroll.name: War Scroll
aka: War of the Sons of Light Against the Sons of Darkness
war-scroll.note: A Qumran text, copied in the first century BC, describing the final war between the sons of light and the sons of darkness, with God's angels fighting on the side of the faithful.

gospel-of-the-hebrews.name: Gospel of the Hebrews
gospel-of-the-hebrews.note: A lost Jewish-Christian gospel of the second century, known only from quotations in Clement of Alexandria, Origen, Jerome and others. Scholars disagree on whether these quotations come from one, two or three gospels. Some of the quotations Jerome gives under this name are now usually assigned to the Gospel of the Nazarenes.

4q521.name: Messianic Apocalypse (4Q521)
4q521.note: A fragmentary Hebrew text from Qumran Cave 4 (first century BC) that says heaven and earth will listen to God's anointed and that the Lord will heal the wounded, raise the dead and bring good news to the poor.

didascalia-apostolorum.name: Didascalia Apostolorum
didascalia-apostolorum.note: A church order written in Greek in Syria in the 200s, surviving mainly in Syriac; it tells the story of Jesus and a woman accused of sin (compare John 7:53–8:11) to urge bishops to receive repentant sinners.

book-of-mormon.name: Book of Mormon
book-of-mormon.note: Scripture, alongside the Bible, for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and other churches of the Latter Day Saint movement (such as Community of Christ), published by Joseph Smith in 1830; in 3 Nephi 15:21 the risen Jesus tells people in the Americas that they are the "other sheep" of John 10:16. It is not part of any Bible.

gospel-of-judas.name: Gospel of Judas
gospel-of-judas.note: A Gnostic gospel of the 100s, known to Irenaeus and found in a Coptic copy of about AD 300, published in 2006, in which Judas alone understands Jesus.

acts-of-pilate.name: Acts of Pilate
acts-of-pilate.note: A Greek account of Jesus's trial, death and descent to the dead (400s in its present form), later part of the Gospel of Nicodemus; it presents Pilate favorably.

acts-of-peter.name: Acts of Peter
acts-of-peter.note: A Greek story of Peter's preaching and contests in Rome (late 100s), known mainly from a Latin manuscript at Vercelli; its account of his martyrdom also survives in Greek. It tells of the "Quo vadis?" meeting and of Peter crucified head downward at his own request.

gospel-of-mary.name: Gospel of Mary
gospel-of-mary.note: A second-century Christian writing, surviving in fragments in Coptic (the Berlin Codex) and Greek, in which Mary Magdalene teaches the disciples what the risen Savior revealed to her and Peter disputes her authority.

gospel-of-philip.name: Gospel of Philip
gospel-of-philip.note: A third-century collection of Gnostic sayings in Coptic, found at Nag Hammadi in 1945, which calls Mary Magdalene Jesus' "companion" and says he often kissed her; the text is damaged at that point.
